items.workarounds: An 'Unarmed: damage die' tweak set to 4; the rest noted in Notes.

verified.note: Species traits aren't processed. The 'Unarmed: damage die' tweak can set the die, but nothing can make unarmed strikes finesse (use Dex). Needed: a species/feature effect that sets the unarmed die and the finesse ability (+5 to hit, 1d4+3 for Tomas). Wookiee Claws can use the same mechanism.

items.resolution: Species natural weapons set the unarmed die (Zabrak and Twi'lek d4, Cathar d6, Wookiee Claws d4). With finesse, the attack and damage use Dexterity when it's better; the Ability column says 'Dexterity (finesse)'. Kadro: +5, 1d4+5 with Brute Force.

items.title: Shield AC counted although the Guardian lists no shield proficiency
items.story: When I equip a shield, I want the sheet to tell me if I'm not proficient (or the class data to list shields), so that my AC is right by the rules.
items.evidence: Guardian proficiencies: 'Armor: Light armor, medium armor' (no shields). Yet the class equipment offers 'a light or medium physical shield'. The sheet's AC is 15 'Mesh armor, Light physical shield', including the shield's +1, with no remark.
items.repro: Guardian with a Light physical shield equipped.
items.expected: Either confirm Guardian shield proficiency in SW5E's data, or show a 'not proficient' warning on the shield.

verified.note: Probably correct. No SW5E class lists shields in armorProficiencies (Fighter 'All armor', Guardian 'Light armor, medium armor'), and the Guardian's own starting equipment offers 'a light or medium physical shield'. So shields appear to follow armor weight. Confirm against the PHB Equipment chapter. Separately, the sheet never checks armor or shield proficiency at all; a general 'not proficient' warning would be S.

items.title: No warning for a two-handed weapon used with a shield
items.story: When I equip a two-handed weapon and a shield, I want a warning, so that a beginner doesn't break the rules.
items.evidence: The Vibroaxe ('heavy, two-handed') and a Light physical shield were equipped at the same time. The attack rolled without comment and AC counted the shield (15). The GM caught it after the round.
items.repro: Equip the Vibroaxe and a shield, then attack.
items.expected: A warning when equipping or attacking.
items.workarounds: Unequipped the shield after the fight.

verified.note: Nothing checks two-handed weapons against an equipped shield, though armorState already knows when a shield is equipped. Warn when equipping either one and on the attack card.

items.resolution: Equipping a shield with a two-handed weapon (or the reverse) says 'Vibroaxe is two-handed and the Light physical shield takes a hand: you can't attack with it while the shield is equipped.' The weapon row gets a 'two-handed + shield' chip and its attack roll the same warning. Nothing is blocked.

items.title: Carrying capacity ignores Powerful Build and Brawny
items.story: When I have Powerful Build and Brawny, I want my carrying capacity tripled, so that encumbrance is right.
items.evidence: Carrying capacity shows Max 255 lb / Push 510 lb at Str 17 and 270/540 at Str 18. Powerful Build doubles it, and Brawny says 'If it would already double, it instead triples.'
items.repro: A Wookiee with Brawny → Combat & Vitals → Carrying capacity.
items.expected: Max 810 lb at Str 18.

verified.note: Carrying capacity is SW5E's c.carryingCapacity, which ignores Powerful Build (255 lb = 17 × 15), and species traits aren't processed. Add a ×2 or ×3 effect on carryingCapacity.*; those numbers can already be changed by effects.

items.resolution: Powerful Build and Brawny each double carrying capacity and push/drag/lift; together they triple them (Rorrwaak: 300 → 900 lb). The ×3 and its sources are shown next to the numbers.

items.title: 0 damage on a hit: is there a minimum in SW5E?
items.story: When my hit's damage comes to 0 after a −1 Str modifier, I want to know whether SW5E has a minimum, so that I apply the rule correctly.
items.evidence: 'Vibrostaff damage: 1 – 1 damage bonus = 0 Kinetic', shown without comment.
items.repro: A character with Str 8 hits with a Vibrostaff and rolls a 1.
items.expected: Either a minimum of 1, or a note that 0 is correct by the rules.

verified.note: SW5E follows 5e: there's no minimum damage of 1, so 1 − 1 = 0 is correct. A small related gap: the damage roll sets no minimum, so with a −2 modifier and a 1 rolled the dock would show −1. Clamp damage at 0 and show a short note.

items.resolution: Not a rules bug (no minimum damage in SW5E); damage rolls now stop at 0 instead of going negative.

items.title: Operative 1's Expertise missing from the builder and sw5e.com's sheet
items.story: When I add Operative 1, I want Expertise listed with Sneak Attack, so that the character data is complete and a future level-up in the extension includes it.
items.evidence: The Operative table says '1st: Expertise, Sneak Attack'. The builder's Operative 1 CLASS FEATURES shows only Sneak Attack, and the site's features list has no Expertise. The sheet fills it in ('Expertise — Levels 1, 6 — from class text'), so only the builder and site are wrong. Tomas logged it high at first and lowered it once he saw the sheet's fill-in.
items.repro: Builder → ADD NEW CLASS → Operative → Class features.
items.expected: Keep the sheet's fill-in, and include Expertise in the in-extension level-up (W-007).

verified.note: The sheet already fills in Expertise from the class text (marked 'from class text', with a 'Your choices' box); only sw5e.com's builder and sheet leave it out. Include Expertise in the planned level-up inside the extension (W-007).

items.title: Togruta shows a Darkvision trait that SW5E's species rules don't list
items.story: When I read my species traits, I want only the traits SW5E's species page lists (or data-only ones flagged), so that I don't wonder whether I have darkvision.
items.evidence: The Species card lists a 'Darkvision' trait (with the 60 ft text), but the Togruta rules page has no darkvision. Vision shows 'Normal', which is correct. sw5e.com's feature list has DARKVISION too. Tomas saw the same for Zabrak (W-141), so fixing W-141 must not turn these into real darkvision.
items.repro: Load a Togruta → Species > Traits (10).
items.expected: Hide or flag data-only traits that the species text doesn't grant.

verified.note: In dev/dumps/rules.json, SW5E's species traits for Togruta and Zabrak have no Darkvision, but SW5E's features data lists one for both, and the engine's feature list is what the Species card shows. Cross-check the engine's traits against the species page's traits and flag extras as 'not in the species rules'. W-141's fix must use the species traits.

items.resolution: Senses and defenses come from SW5E's species rules, so the data-only Darkvision of Togruta and Zabrak isn't shown (still worth reporting upstream).

items.title: Stimpac 'only one at a time' rule: check it's enforced and shown
items.story: When I use a second stim while one is active, I want the sheet to replace the older one or refuse, as 'A creature can benefit from only one stimpac at a time' says.
items.evidence: The Strength Stim text says 'A creature can benefit from only one stimpac at a time.' Untested, because she had only one stim. The code has a 'replaces … (only one at a time)' message, so it may already work; needs a check.
items.repro: Use two different stims on yourself.
items.expected: The older stim is replaced, with a note.

verified.where: effects.js (group from 'only one … at a time'); viewer.js:startEffect, useItem, receiveEffect
verified.note: Already enforced. effects.js reads 'only one stimpac at a time' into the group 'stimpac', startEffect ends the older effect in the same group, and useItem and receiveEffect say 'It replaces … (only one at a time).' No change needed beyond a test.

items.resolution: Already enforced (only one stimpac at a time, with a message).

items.title: Ability breakdown lumps species, ASI and feat bonuses together
items.story: When I check my Strength, I want '+1 Togruta, +2 ASI (Guardian 4)' as separate lines, so that I can audit the number.
items.evidence: The Str card reads 'base 15 · +3 from species/ASIs/feats/tweaks'.
items.repro: Abilities → STR on a character with a species bonus and an ASI.
items.expected: One line per source.

verified.note: The breakdown shows 'base N' and one lumped '+X from species/ASIs/feats/tweaks'; only effects are listed one by one. Split it using raw.species.abilityScoreImprovement, each class's abilityScoreImprovements (with class and level), feats and tweaks.

items.resolution: Each ability score lists its increases one by one: '+2 Wookiee · +2 ASI (Berserker 4) · +1 from Brawny (tweak)', then effects; anything unexplained is 'other'.

items.title: Clearing a tweak's value deletes the tweak and shifts the rows (typing goes into another tweak)
items.story: When I clear one field of a tweak to change it, I want the tweak kept (or an Undo) and the rows to stay put, so that I don't lose a tweak or overwrite another tweak's reason.
items.evidence: Sam cleared the AC tweak's 'Set to 14' value. The AC tweak vanished at once (8 → 7 tweaks), with no message and no undo. The page shifted, and his next typing went into Piloting's reason: 'Mercenary background skill' was replaced with 'Wookiee Hide (13 + Dex) is 1 better than Unarmored Defense…'.
items.repro: Tweaks table → a 'set to' tweak → select and delete its value → click the same row's Bonus box and type.
items.expected: The tweak stays until removed with ×, or a 'Tweak removed · Undo' toast appears. No layout jump.
items.workarounds: Restored Piloting's reason by hand and re-added AC as 'add 1'.

verified.note: Clearing 'Set to' makes updateTweak store override: null. fxTweakLeaves counts a value as a tweak only if one of its fields is not an object, and typeof null is 'object', so { override: null } drops out of the list. The row vanishes, the tweak stays stored (with its reason) but can't be removed, the rows shift up, and the next click and typing land in another tweak (Piloting's reason). Fix: treat null as empty, keep the row until × is pressed, and offer Undo.

items.resolution: A cleared field keeps the tweak (shown as 'no change' until removed with ×), so rows don't shift.

items.title: Short 'first session' guide for new players
items.story: When I open the sheet for my first game ever, I want a short guide (roll a check, attack, take damage, rage, use a medpac, rest), so that I don't have to read a dense feature reference.
items.evidence: The README's 'Use' section is a series of very long bullets; the Combat & Vitals / Edit / inventory / Use bullet is one paragraph of about 120 words. From it, Sam picked out only Load from SW5E, Start for Rage, Use for medpacs and 'click a number to roll'.
items.repro: Open sw5e-sheet/README.md as a new player.
items.expected: A 6–8 step 'Your first session' section, or an in-sheet help card.

verified.note: There is no beginner guide; the README's 'Use' section is a set of very long bullets. Add a 6–8 step 'Your first session' section (roll a check, attack, take damage, start Rage, use a medpac, rest), or an in-sheet help card.

items.resolution: README starts with 'Your first session' (8 steps: get your character, roll, attack, take damage or heal, use a feature, cast a power, use an item, rest), and the same guide is in the sheet: More ▾ (or ☰ on phones) → First session guide.

items.title: Explain weapon properties on hover
items.story: When I see 'heavy, two-handed' or 'versatile (2d4)', I want to hover or tap it to read what it means, so that I learn the rules as a new player.
items.evidence: The weapons table shows Vibroaxe 'Dexterity 11, heavy, two-handed' and Vibrospear 'Thrown (range 25/75), versatile (2d4)' with no tooltip. Sam didn't know that two-handed rules out a shield (W-149).
items.repro: Hover a property in Weapons & Attacks or Equipment.
items.expected: A short rule text per property.

verified.note: SW5E's weapon and armor property texts are already downloaded with the rules data (bridge.js fetches them) but never used; the sheet prints only property names. Add hover/tap explanations from that data.

items.resolution: Weapon and armor properties in Weapons & Attacks and Equipment explain themselves on hover, focus or tap, from SW5E's rules text ('Two-Handed: A weapon with this property requires two hands to use.').

items.title: Damage-die tweak: '1d4' becomes 14, and the die can be saved empty
items.story: When I set a damage die with a tweak, I want to type '1d4', 'd4' or '4' and have it kept, so that Claws or Unarmed Combatant work on the first try.
items.evidence: The Add row's amount box says 'e.g. 1' and is numeric. Typing '1d4' gave 14, and the row showed an empty 'Die' box; typing '4' worked ('1d4 Kinetic') (Tomas). Sam chose 'set to' + 4 and the tweak was added with an EMPTY 'Die' box. The row's tooltip 'Damage die size, e.g. 6 for d6' only appears after adding, and the mode list offers proficient/expertise for a damage die. Sam rated it medium, Tomas low.
items.repro: Settings, Tweaks & Data → Add a tweak to… Unarmed: damage die → set to → type 1d4 (or 4) → reason → Add.
items.expected: The die is saved. The box is labelled as a die size ('d'), accepts d4/1d4/4, and only sensible modes are offered.
items.workarounds: Typed 4, or typed it again into the row's Die box.

verified.note: The Add row's amount box is a number input, so typing '1d4' becomes 14. For 'Unarmed: damage die', addTweak stores { override: n } or { bonus: n }, but the tweak row shows and edits the dieSize field ('Die'), which therefore stays empty. Fix: for damage-die targets offer only 'die size', accept d4 / 1d4 / 4, and store dieSize.

items.resolution: A damage-die tweak takes 'd4', '1d4' or '4' (the box says 'die, e.g. d4') and stores the die size.

items.title: No warning when an AC 'set to' tweak overrides armor or a shield
items.story: When I equip a shield while an AC 'set to' tweak exists, I want a warning, so that my AC doesn't silently ignore the shield.
items.evidence: With 'AC set to 14', equipping a Light physical shield (AC +1) left AC at 14. The hover read 'Without tweaks or effects: 12 → now 14 · = 14 AC …'.
items.repro: Add an AC set-to tweak, then equip a shield.
items.expected: A notice: 'your AC tweak overrides the shield's +1'.

verified.note: Nothing warns when an AC 'set to' tweak hides an armor or shield change; only the hover shows '= 14'. Warn when equipping, or show 'your AC tweak overrides the shield's +1' next to AC.

items.resolution: With an AC 'set to' tweak, AC shows 'set to 14 by a tweak', and equipping armor or a shield says 'Your AC tweak sets AC to 14, so the Light physical shield doesn't change it: change the tweak to a bonus, or remove it.'

items.title: Enter in the tweak Reason box doesn't add the tweak
items.story: When I've typed a tweak's reason, I want Enter to add it, so that adding several tweaks is quicker.
items.evidence: Settings, Tweaks & Data > Add a tweak to… > fill in > Enter in the Reason box: nothing happened; they had to click Add. Tomas hit the same while making his skill tweaks (W-024).
items.repro: Fill in a tweak row and press Enter in the Reason field.
items.expected: Enter adds the tweak.

verified.note: The Enter key is handled for the add-item and effect boxes but not for the Add-a-tweak row. Make Enter in the Reason or amount box add the tweak.

items.resolution: Enter in the Add-a-tweak amount or reason box adds the tweak.

items.title: Tweak target list is one flat 65-entry select
items.story: When I pick what to tweak, I want a grouped or searchable list, so that typing 'AC' finds AC.
items.evidence: 'Add a tweak to…' is a single flat select of 65 entries. Typing 'AC' selects 'Acrobatics (DEX)', and AC is 17 entries further down.
items.repro: Add a tweak to… → type AC.
items.expected: Optgroups (Abilities / Skills / Combat / Powers / Weapons) or a search box.

verified.note: The list is one flat select: ability scores, saves and skills first, AC later. Typing 'AC' jumps to 'Acrobatics (DEX)'. Group the options (Combat / Abilities / Saves / Skills / Powers / Weapons), with Combat first, or use a searchable box.

items.resolution: The tweak target list is grouped: Combat (AC first), Ability scores, Saving throws, Skills (alphabetical), Powers, Maneuvers, Weapons. Typing 'AC' finds AC.
